model_annotation: This line chart, titled “Veterans as share of population,” illustrates the percentage of veterans within the total U.S. population from 1960 to 2010. The horizontal axis represents years, marked at regular intervals from 1960 to 2010, with no explicit scale type indicated but appearing linear. The vertical axis represents the percentage share, scaled linearly from 0 to 15%, with labeled tick marks at 0, 5, 10, and 15%. A single red line with circular markers connects data points, starting at 12.8% in 1960, rising to 13.8% in 1970, then declining to 12.1% in 1980, 11.0% in 1990, 9.4% in 2000, and finally 7% in 2010. The chart source is cited as the Census Bureau and Pew Research Center.

model_annotations.English: This line chart, titled "Veterans as share of population," illustrates the percentage of the U.S. population that are veterans from 1960 to 2010, with data sourced from the Census Bureau and presented by the Pew Research Center. The x-axis represents the year, marked at 10-year intervals from 1960 to 2010. The y-axis represents the percentage of the population, scaled linearly from 0% to 15%, with major gridlines and labels at 0, 5, 10, and 15%. A single red line with circular markers traces the trend: it begins at 12.8% in 1960, rises to a peak of 13.8% in 1970, then declines steadily to 7% by 2010, with intermediate values shown as 12.1% in 1980, 11.0% in 1990, and 9.4% in 2000.
